newsitem.title: UK: UK financial services reform to start now - Brown.
newsitem.headline: UK financial services reform to start now - Brown.

text.p: British Chancellor of the Exchequer Gordon Brown said on Tuesday that reforms to UK financial services regulation should start at once.
Brown said the current division of responsibility between the Security and Investments Board (SIB) and the self regulatory organisations was inefficient and confusing for investors.
"Reform is long overdue to simplify the delivery of financial services regulation," Brown told Parliament.
"I can announce today that work is to start immediately on the legislation needed to simply and reform the regulatory system at an early opportunity," Brown said.

He said supervision for Britain's banking sector would be transfered from the Bank of England to the Security and Investment Board (SIB). "The SIB will become the single regulator, underpinned by statute," he said in a statement to the House of Commons.

"Responsibility for banking supervision will be transferred...from the Bank of England to a new and strengthened Securities and Investment Board, which will also, as a result of forthcoming legislation take direct responsibility for the regulatory regime covered by the Financial Services Act," Brown said.

But that did not go far enough, Britain's new Chancellor said. In today's world of integrated global markets, he said the distinctions between different types of financial institutions were becoming blurred.
"So there is a strong case in principle for bringing the regulation of banking, securities and insurance together under one roof," he said.
Brown paid tribute to the current SIB chairman Sir Andrew Large, who he said had decided to step down.
And he pledged that his reforms would put the public interest first and increase public confidence in the system.

"My reforms are essential to ensure the future confidence of investors large and small, and the future success of the increasingly integrated financial services industry on which so many jobs rely," Brown said.
